claim: None of the exactly eight residual incidence-complex orbits for H9/14 second-layer record 17 is the nerve of a compact hyperbolic Coxeter polytope; hence the whole graph shadow is compact-Coxeter impossible.

independent_hostile_replay.method: no production imports; independent 9+5 Lanner representative closure, finite Coxeter classifier, nerve reconstruction, and incremental actual-vertex replay

compact_inputs: Every order-four/five minimal nonface of a compact Coxeter nerve supports a classical Lanner diagram.
Every actual rank-nine vertex diagram of a compact Coxeter polytope is elliptic.
The complete classical Lanner tables have 108 and 420 labelled placements in orders four and five.
The frozen whole-shadow theorem leaves exactly the eight audited incidence-complex orbits and no others.
proof.finite_search: For each orbit, join the complete Lanner placement tables on the listed decisive supports and replay every restriction induced by every actual rank-nine face. Five orbits have zero elliptic states after three supports; the other three have 18, 8, and 18 states after three supports and zero after the fourth.
proof.perron_frobenius_step: On any actual-vertex restriction write the normalized Coxeter Gram matrix as G=I-A, where A is symmetric and entrywise nonnegative. G is positive definite exactly when lambda_max(A)=rho(A)<1. Replacing an unforced right angle by any finite non-right angle gives A'>=A entrywise, hence rho(A')>=rho(A). A sparse restriction that is already non-elliptic therefore cannot become elliptic. This proves that incremental sparse-shadow pruning is lossless.
proof.why_no_global_gram_search_is_needed: Every possible finite Coxeter labeling already fails a necessary positive-definite principal vertex condition.
